decisions.reason: Although it draws on core wafer-processing capabilities, after several years with no visible follow-up and without flagship status management can more easily justify ending it and reallocating resources.
Its close fit with the firm's carrier-handling direction, the public launch, and the likelihood that weak demand can be read as temporary still favor continued commitment.
As a publicly presented flagship technology closely tied to the firm's announced move toward more complex packaging wafers, management is likely to persist despite uncertain traction.
Because the firm publicly created a brand around this line and it stays very close to the established glass and quartz business, escalation of commitment strongly supports retention.

This product is comparatively distant from the core offer and less visibly central to the firm's declared strategy, so disappointing results would be harder for management to justify carrying forward.
